proof_summary: For \(k>60\), set \(n=2k+1\); if \(4k+2\) had no two-prime decomposition, then every symmetric candidate pair indexing the matrix would fail to be simultaneously prime (their sum is \(2n=4k+2\)), so the matrix would be zero and its determinant would vanish, contradicting the hypothesis. The cases \(1\le k\le60\) are settled by an explicit finite list of prime decompositions.
